title: New defaults, water and cloud directions, and texture packs
intro: Your round 3 answers are now the defaults: round 2's golden hour and leaves, round 2's lively sunset water, a new moon at 0.25 and the warmer torches. The orange cone below the sun is gone. It came from the aerial-perspective term, not the water, and is fixed whether aerial is on or off. Also fixed: river water is clear and neutral instead of cyan, river_noon's highlight no longer clips, and the near-water flecks are back at about half of round 3. Not in this round, on purpose: the sun-core sparkle and the stronger motes were built and rendered, but in the critic's check (and mine) they still look identical to off, so showing them would repeat round 3's "these all look the exact same". They come back once they read clearly in a still frame. The last three questions are directions to choose together: water from other packs' approaches (links only, plus real photos), cloud inspiration (photos) and a texture pack. Every render shows its cost per frame on High at 1440p. The budget is 3 ms; the dearest frame here is about 1.05 ms.

scenes.name: Golden hour: round 2's look, now the default
scenes.question: Your B pick from round 3 is the default again (no extra amber on lit faces). You said the horizon band is pretty flat: the critic agrees, and that band is the next golden-hour job. Is this the base to build on?
scenes.notePrompt: Right base? What should the horizon band do: more gold, more colour bands, clouds?

options.label: New default
options.critic: Critic 6: Lit ridge faces are a nice amber against the shade. The horizon band is still a flat beige strip, and the grass in front is dull dark green.

scenes.name: Leaves: round 2's look, now the default
scenes.question: The same clearing as round 3, with round 2's leaves (your B). The critic notes that the forest_golden view lost round 3's warm light shaft through the trees along with the extra amber.
scenes.notePrompt: Right? Do you want a warm shaft of light through gaps in the canopy, without the amber on every leaf?

options.label: New default
options.critic: Critic 6: Sunlit leaves at upper right and the birch highlight read well; the ground is one dark green mass.

scenes.name: Sunset water: lively, the cone fixed
scenes.question: Round 2's lively water (your A), in the view where the sun is clear of the cliff. The orange cone is gone.
scenes.notePrompt: Is this balanced? What should happen right under the sun?

options.label: New default
options.critic: Critic 7: Cone gone. The sun path is a soft amber band mid-frame on neutral glassy grey-teal water. The bottom third is flat dark green with no depth gradient.

scenes.name: New moon at 0.25
scenes.question: Your B from round 3, now the default.
scenes.notePrompt: Still the deep, rich dark you picked? The critic would like the sky a touch more navy.

options.label: New default
options.critic: Critic 6: Deep dark with stars (mean brightness 0.037), sand and water readable. The sky is near-black rather than visibly navy; the dirt is nearly lost.

scenes.name: Warmer torches, now the default
scenes.question: Your B from round 3. Heat shimmer, embers and torch dust are on the list but not built yet.
scenes.notePrompt: Warm enough? Which comes first: heat shimmer, embers or dust?

options.label: New default
options.critic: Critic 7: Warm tungsten-to-candle falloff on the planks reads as flame light; corners dark but legible.

scenes.name: Extreme Hills: aerial perspective, without the cone
scenes.question: Aerial perspective (distant land fading into the air's colour) is fixed: it no longer paints the sun's glow below the sun. A is the default (off), B has it on. The critic thinks neither fixes the scene: the colour range itself (pale mint grass, flat mountains, empty sky) is the problem, and the texture-pack and cloud questions below bear on it.
scenes.notePrompt: Is the depth in B worth the haze? What would you change about the colours here?

options.label: Aerial off (default)
options.critic: Critic 4: Pale mint-grey grass, an empty sky gradient and flat orange-grey mountains: still bland.

options.label: Aerial on
options.critic: Critic 4: Adds some depth, but the haze turns the mountains pinkish-grey and the left valley milky: it washes out a colour range you already dislike.

scenes.name: Glassy rivers and lakes, murky swamp
scenes.question: You agreed with round 3's critic, so: river and lake water is now clear and neutral instead of cyan, the noon highlight no longer clips, and swamp water was pushed towards murky olive. The critic says the swamp is still too clear and the river highlight still too milky.
scenes.notePrompt: Which is off, and how? How murky should a swamp be?

options.label: River at noon (glassy)
options.critic: Critic 5: No longer clipping, but a large milky-white smear still dominates the bottom-centre. The ledges seen through the water show as salmon-orange stripes.

ref.credit: amanderson2, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
ref.title: Clear River water Bled Vintgar Slovenia (8095482709).jpg

options.label: Lake at noon (glassy)
options.critic: Critic 7: Neutral, clear lake water with a good sand island and reflections; a touch slate-teal at front left.

options.label: Swamp (murky olive)
options.critic: Critic 5: Less jade than round f, but the shallows are still clear grass-green, not murky olive: you see the bottom sharply. The far water is pale cyan-white.

scenes.name: Near-water flecks at half
scenes.question: You said round 3's flecks were a bit much, and that round 2's amount, or a little more, was right. A has none (the default since round 3), B has them at about half of round 3.
scenes.notePrompt: Is B the amount you meant? More, fewer?

options.label: No flecks (default)
options.critic: Critic 8: Deep saturated blue with a turquoise shoal at right: the best of the set. Slightly plain without flecks.

options.label: Flecks at half
options.critic: Critic 8: A few more faint flecks in the near blue add a little life without clutter. Marginally better than without.

scenes.name: Water: which direction?
scenes.question: You asked to look at other packs' water and decide together. We don't show their screenshots, but their own pages are linked below. Broadly, packs pick one of three looks, shown here with real photos: a calm mirror with one soft sun path; a broken field of glitter on choppy water; or cool, clear water with a narrow path. D is ours today. Pick a direction (or say which pack's water you like on its page).
scenes.notePrompt: Which direction? Any pack whose water you love, and what about it?

links.note: lists waves, reflections, refraction and water fog; water colour and waves are adjustable
stylised; offers a more realistic water style as an option
realism-leaning, with a fully revamped sky, lighting and water
the classic vivid look (we compare against it in testing)

options.label: Calm mirror, one soft path
options.desc: Still water mirrors the sky; the sun makes one soft, smooth path. Quiet and cinematic.

options.label: Broken glitter field
options.desc: Choppy water breaks the sun into thousands of sharp glints: lively and bright, harder to get right.

ref.credit: Pdpics, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

options.label: Cool and clear, narrow path
options.desc: Cooler, clearer water with a narrow broken path under the sun; you see into the shallows.

options.label: Ours today (lively)

options.desc: Round 2's lively water, the current default, refined from here.

scenes.name: Clouds: which inspiration?
scenes.question: You asked for cloud inspiration before we build any. Four directions, as real photos, plus none. Real volumetric clouds are a bigger, dearer job, so this picks the look first.
scenes.notePrompt: Which sky? Mixed by weather or time of day? How much of the sky should they cover?

options.label: Fair-weather cumulus
options.desc: Scattered puffy white clouds with flat bases over a blue sky, casting shadows on the land.

ref.credit: Toby Hudson, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
ref.title: Cumulus humilis clouds.jpg

options.label: High wispy cirrus
options.desc: Thin, feathery streaks high up. Cheap, catches sunset colour, never blocks the sun.

ref.credit: ADARSHluck, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
ref.title: Cirrus uncinus clouds in the morning sky.jpg

options.label: Altocumulus sheet
options.desc: A mid-level layer of small rounded puffs, a 'mackerel sky' that glows at sunrise and sunset.

ref.credit: LivingShadow, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
ref.title: Altocumulus clouds - 2004.jpg

options.label: Dramatic broken clouds
options.desc: Dark broken clouds with the sun behind them and rays fanning out: moody and cinematic.

ref.credit: Brocken Inaglory, retouched by User:Flamurai, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
ref.title: Sunset clouds and crepuscular rays over pacific edit.jpg

options.label: No clouds
options.desc: A clear sky; put the effort into light, colour and depth instead.

scenes.name: Texture pack: which way?
scenes.question: You suggested working on a texture pack in parallel. Images of other texture packs are not shown here: some are all-rights-reserved, and the site is public. Four routes, with what their licences allow:
scenes.notePrompt: Which route? Any pack you already like or dislike?

links.note: licence: https://faithfulpack.net/license (use, modify, redistribute with credit and a link)
64x, all rights reserved, no public redistribution
32x, all rights reserved; link to the official download only

options.label: Faithful-based
options.desc: Start from Faithful 32x, whose licence lets us change it and ship it with credit, and extend it to the modded and custom blocks. A solid, vanilla-faithful base at double resolution.

options.label: Keep vanilla style
options.desc: Stay with 16x vanilla-style textures (our custom blocks already match them) and let the shaders carry the look. No licence questions, least work.

options.label: Sample the others first
options.desc: Try Soartex Invictus, Conquest_ and John Smith Legacy in a private test client to find what you like, then build our own in that spirit. They are all-rights-reserved, so they can't ship in the pack or appear on this site.

options.label: A custom pack from scratch
options.desc: Our own textures for everything. The most control, but by far the most work, and it extends the whole process.
